ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A source is supplying a load through a 2-phase, 3-wire transmission system as shown in the <image>. The instantaneous voltage and current in phase-a are \( V_{an} = 220\sin(100\pi t) \, V \) and \( i_a = 10\sin(100\pi t) \, A \), respectively. Similarly, for phase-b, the instantaneous voltage and current are \( V_{bn} = 220\cos(100\pi t) \, V \) and \( i_b = 10\cos(100\pi t) \, A \), respectively.

The total instantaneous power flowing from the source to the load is:

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is Source, on the right side is Load, and in the middle there are three wires, labeled a, b, n, corresponding to the load-end a′, b′, n′, forming a 2-phase, 3-wire system. The current arrows i_a, i_b on phase a and phase b both point from the source to the load, and the voltages V_an and V_bn both use the neutral line n as the reference, respectively corresponding to the two power supply branches a-n and b-n. Reasoning: The total instantaneous power is the sum of the instantaneous power transmitted to the load by the two phase lines. phase-a: p_a = V_an i_a = [220 sin(100πt)][10 sin(100πt)] = 2200 sin^2(100πt). phase-b: p_b = V_bn i_b = [220 cos(100πt)][10 cos(100πt)] = 2200 cos^2(100πt). Therefore p_total = p_a + p_b = 2200[sin^2(100πt) + cos^2(100πt)] = 2200 W.
